findings.failure_condition: When a source payload contains an own JSON __proto__ key with an object value, normalizeJsonValue assigns it into result = {}. JavaScript invokes the legacy prototype setter instead of creating an own enumerable property, so stableStringify/JSON.stringify omits the key and the event fact is lost from canonical storage after publish/reopen.
findings.required_behavior: Preserve every valid JSON object key, including __proto__, as an own data property through normalization, canonical serialization, publication, and reopen, without mutating the result prototype.

test_assessment.applicability: Applicable: the cumulative change contains product runtime behavior and tests.
test_assessment.boundary: The real Gateway/WebSocket route is exercised with an injected provider/store interface, while SQLite durability/reopen is tested separately. Recorded Owner/IPC and Android suites cover the frozen regression boundary.
test_assessment.necessity: The frozen product-history and IPC/Owner JVM validations target acceptance and protected regressions. No tests were run during this review.
test_assessment.oracle: The current product contract specifies preservation of unknown JSON fields, bounded paging/detail, and IPC authority; assertions exercise projected fields and request routing. The __proto__ key case is not covered.
test_assessment.reason: S3 adds product-history provider and Gateway behavior, and modifies S1 payload preservation plus an existing serializer; recorded evidence covers product-history acceptance and protected IPC/Owner and Android JVM regressions.
test_assessment.reuse: Recorded evidence reuses the S3 product-history suite and existing S1 Rust conformance/blocker checks, with three current execution validation references. No additional tests were run.
